title: Latchline
hook: Hold to latch a tiny courier to the next overhead rail, release to sling across the gap, and risk one more delivery before banking the run.
audience: Arcade players who like immediate retries, short mastery sessions and a visible risk-versus-safety choice.
core_loop: Time a latch, build a swing, release through a delivery gate, choose a safer bank gate or a harder bonus route, then retry a sixty-second course with a local best score.

score_notes.demand: A low-priced score-attack comparable is on sale; that is weak indirect evidence for this control scheme and audience.
score_notes.distinctiveness: Tether games already exist; the delivery-versus-bank choice needs a close competitor search before claiming meaningful novelty.
score_notes.fun_potential: Control feel and readability dominate the pitch and have not been tested.
score_notes.scope_fit: A side-view course and one input keep the proposed prototype small, conditional on stable, readable movement.
score_notes.distribution: A successful risky delivery might be understandable in a short clip, but no creator/player response has been measured.

evidence.claim: The inspected US/English listing offered Superflight at USD 2.99 and displayed user reviews. This is a dated visible offer, not its realized receipt, lifetime pricing, sales volume or a recommended Latchline price.

The developer describes brief score-chasing sessions and riskier proximity manoeuvres. That supports a compact arcade comparable; the source does not validate tether controls or our delivery mechanic.

risks: Movement can feel frustrating unless attachment selection, release timing and collision feedback are consistent.
The score loop may become repetitive without excellent feel and varied but readable routes.
Competition from free browser and mobile arcade games may weaken willingness to pay.
Local scoring avoids online service work, but may reduce the appeal to competitive players.
This is not a trend finding; two records from one listing are not independent sources. Working title and originality are unverified.
next_test: If authorized, build a side-view greybox with one input, a ten-second practice section and one sixty-second course. Observe five arcade players. Continue if four complete a latch-release-delivery sequence within two minutes without coaching and three voluntarily restart at least twice; record missed-input causes and ask whether banking changed a decision. If control confusion dominates, fix feel before adding content.
decision_reason: Held as an evergreen control experiment. The broad trend-first run did not establish a natural rising-topic origin; existing mechanics and evidence remain available.
commercial_hypothesis: Test a very small premium PC arcade game and a browser-playable sample. USD 2.99-4.99 is only a price hypothesis pending content and audience tests; a full free browser release would require a different commercial case.

prototype_envelope.scope: One course, one input, explicit attachment preview, bank gate, instant retry and local score; no online leaderboard, upgrades or level editor.

budget_note: Unvalidated prototype estimate, excluding participant recruitment, final movement polish, art/audio, commercial content, marketing, compatibility QA and release lead time. No spend authorized.

decision_history.reason: Created as an active arcade alternative; not selected.
